title: Algolia secured API key: the derived value against its parent key
summary: A secured API key (the base64 of an HMAC and a URL-encoded parameter list) delivered to a frontend, and the parent API key that is the secret input of its construction.
rationale: Claim secured-api-key-construction-documented records the construction: a SHA-256 HMAC with the parent API key as the secret over the URL-encoded parameters, concatenated with them and base64-encoded. Claim secured-api-key-frontend-delivery records that the derived value is generated on the backend and handed to frontends and mobile apps. The secret input (the parent key, a main key of an unspecified role) and the derived value are therefore different values with different documented handling. What is open: whether Algolia treats the derived value as confidential, since the restrictions and filters travel inside it (open-question-5), the HMAC encoding and the decoded layout (open-question-4), whether it can be told from a main key by shape (open-questions 3 and 6), and whether the parent key can be recovered from it (open-question-5). No bytes of a secured key can be built without guessing, so no fixture exists. Contract claims cited: secured-api-key/secured-api-key-construction-documented, secured-api-key/secured-api-key-frontend-delivery, secured-api-key/secured-api-key-inherits-restrictions.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Settled by: an Algolia statement of the confidentiality of the derived value, of its encoding and layout, or of whether the parent key is recoverable from it.

sources.supports: Compute a SHA-256 HMAC with: Secret: the parent API key; Message: a URL-encoded list of query parameters. These query parameters are applied to every request that uses the API key and can’t be modified by end users. Concatenate the SHA-256 HMAC with the list of query parameters into a single string. Encode the resulting string in base64.
To prevent this, generate a secured API key on the backend with filters (users can’t alter these filters).
You can get this API key in your frontend from your backend—for example, with an API request.
That’s why we recommend fetching restricted API keys dynamically from your app’s backend.
They inherit the rights and restrictions of their base API keys, which they can’t override. It means you can’t generate a secured API key with fewer restrictions than its base API key.
Secured API keys are virtual, which means they aren’t stored anywhere, and you can’t find them on the Algolia dashboard.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. No expectation is asserted and no value was built: the record states what the cited contract settles and what it leaves open. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
